title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let \hat\Pi_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, with inertia generators l_0, l_1, l_\infty. Let \sigma_\infty be the involution z -> 1-z. It fixes ∞, swaps 0 and 1, and acts on \hat\Pi_{0,3} with \sigma_\infty(l_0) = l_1.

The target \hat\Pi_{0,3}\cdot\{1,\sigma_\infty\} is the semidirect product \hat\Pi_{0,3} ⋊ Z/2. It is the orbifold fundamental group of the quotient [(P^1-{0,1,∞})/<z -> 1-z>]. That quotient has:
- an orbifold point of order 2 (the image of z = 1/2);
- a cusp at ∞;
- a cusp that is the common image of 0 and 1.
As an abstract profinite group it is Z/2 ⨿ \hat Z.

The map \hat\psi_{1/2} (the index 1/2 refers to the fixed point z = 1/2) is a homomorphism from \hat\Pi_{0,3} onto this orbifold group. It sends:
- l_0 to \sigma_\infty (the cusp 0 becomes the order-2 point);
- l_1 to l_1 (the cusp {0,1});
- l_\infty to \varepsilon_\infty (the cusp ∞).
So it is the quotient by the normal closure of l_0^2, identified with \hat\Pi ⋊ Z/2.

Problem. Let u be a Galois-type or Teichmüller-type automorphism of \hat\Pi_{0,3} with u(l_i) = int(g_i) l_i^p, where p ∈ \hat Z^* plays the role of the cyclotomic exponent. Grothendieck asks when u is compatible with \hat\psi, i.e. when \hat\psi∘u = int(·)∘u'∘\hat\psi for an extension u' of u to the orbifold group. The compatibility is written \hat\psi(u(x)) = int(\psi(u)) u \hat\psi(x). He evaluates it on each generator.

(1) x = l_0.
- Since p is odd, \sigma_\infty^p = \sigma_\infty.
- Hence int(\hat\psi(g_0)) fixes \sigma_\infty, so \hat\psi(g_0) centralizes \sigma_\infty.
- The centralizer of the order-2 element in Z/2 ⨿ \hat Z is {1, \sigma_\infty}. So \hat\psi(g_0) = \sigma_\infty^\alpha with α ∈ Z/2.
- α depends on the choice of g_0 modulo L_0 = <l_0>, because l_0 maps to \sigma_\infty.

(2) x = l_1.
- In the same way, \hat\psi(g_1) = g_1 l_1^\beta, using that the centralizer of l_1 in the target is L_1.
- Normalize g_1 by the symmetry: g_1 = \sigma_\infty(g_0 l_0^\gamma) = \sigma_\infty(g_0) l_1^\gamma.
- This gives \hat\psi(\sigma_\infty(g_0)) = \sigma_\infty(g_0) l_1^\beta.
- Put h_0 = \sigma_\infty(g_0)^{-1} g_0 and solve: \hat\psi(h_0) = l_1^{-\beta} h_0 g_0^{-1} \sigma_\infty^\alpha.
- I re-derived this: \sigma^\alpha \hat\psi(h_0)^{-1} = g_0 h_0^{-1} l_1^\beta, which gives the stated formula.

(3) x = l_\infty (bracketed).
- The analogous computation gives \hat\psi(g_\infty) = g_\infty.

What it serves. This is the orbifold or geometric derivation of the 'order-2' (2-cycle) constraint on the Galois/GT-action. The element h_0 = \sigma_\infty(g_0)^{-1} g_0 is the analogue of f(y,x)^{-1} f(x,y) in Drinfeld's notation. Requiring compatibility with the (2,∞,∞) orbifold quotient through z = 1/2 forces relations on (g_0, g_1, g_\infty) that encode the relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1.
errors: The step 'centralizer of \sigma_\infty is {1,\sigma_\infty}' is used without proof. It is true by profinite free-product theory (Herfort–Ribes type results for Z/2 ⨿ \hat Z), but it is a genuine input.
The page uses \sigma_\infty^p = \sigma_\infty silently. This needs p odd, which holds since p ∈ \hat Z^*.

Notation is loose. Elements g_0, h_0 of \hat\Pi_{0,3} are used both in the source and, via the inclusion as an index-2 subgroup, in the target of \hat\psi (which is not that inclusion). The computation is consistent, but this conflation should be flagged.
The extension of u to the target group (the action on \sigma_\infty and \varepsilon_\infty) is assumed, not constructed.
The formula for \hat\psi(h_0) is not reduced further. The intended consequence, a 2-cycle-type relation for h_0, is not explicitly drawn on this page.

ideas.what: Viewing \hat\Pi_{0,3} ⋊ <z -> 1-z> as the orbifold group of signature (2,∞,∞), and the map \hat\psi_{1/2} sending l_0 to the order-2 element, as a structure the Galois/Teichmüller action must respect.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold quotient of P^1-{0,1,∞} by S_2; (2,∞,∞) triangle-type profinite group; geometric origin of GT relation (II)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990 (relation f(x,y)f(y,x)=1); Ihara; Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura in the 1990s for geometric/orbifold interpretations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the action of Gal on the 'tour de Teichmüller' and the need for relations of order 2 and 3, but not this explicit computation.

ideas.what: Determining images of the 'gluing' elements g_i via centralizers of inertia generators: Z(\sigma_\infty) = {1,\sigma_\infty}, Z(l_1) = L_1.
ideas.modern_name: Centralizers of inertia/torsion in profinite free products (Herfort–Ribes); standard lemma in anabelian/GT computations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Herfort–Ribes; used routinely by Ihara, Nakamura

ideas.what: Change-of-normalization bookkeeping: g_1 = \sigma_\infty(g_0) l_1^\gamma, h_0 = \sigma_\infty(g_0)^{-1} g_0, and the formula for \hat\psi(h_0).
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of the GT parameter f via the involution x <-> y

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an explicit orbifold-covering mechanism. Compatibility of an automorphism with the map onto the (2,∞,∞) orbifold group through the point 1/2 is meant to produce the order-2 relation. He stops after computing \hat\psi(g_0), \hat\psi(g_1), \hat\psi(h_0), \hat\psi(g_\infty) without extracting the relation. This viewpoint is known in later literature (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura), so it is mainly of historical interest: Grothendieck was already deriving GT-type relations from orbifold quotients around 1981–82.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents priority and method. Grothendieck derives the 2-cycle constraint from an orbifold quotient map rather than from braid/associator relations, years before Drinfeld's GT (1990).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a coherent early computation of the order-2 compatibility through the orbifold quotient by z -> 1-z, which is of historical interest as pre-Drinfeld. But the mathematics (the 2-cycle relation and its orbifold interpretation) is well established in the later literature, and the page is an unfinished routine computation.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: \sigma_\infty^p should be read as \sigma_\infty because p is odd. The struck-out text on the right of the (int(\hat\psi(g_0)))(\sigma_\infty^p) line is a deleted 'int(g_0)'. The double bar under it indicates that the left side equals \sigma_\infty.
The marginal note in case 2 is better read as 'β ne dépend [que] du choix de g_0 [et de] γ mod L_0' (uncertain), not simply 'β ne dépend que du choix de g_0 mod L_0'.
'g_1 = g\rho(g_0)' is likely a misreading of something like 'g_1 ≡ \sigma_\infty(g_0) ...' or 'g_1 = \sigma_\infty(g_0 l_0^\gamma)'. The handwriting is ambiguous.
Case 1 in the image reads 'u(\hat\psi(x)) = \sigma_\infty' (u applied to \hat\psi(x)), as transcribed.
In the line \hat\psi(g_0 h_0^{-1} l_1^\gamma) = ..., the struck-out item is '\sigma_\infty(g_0)', replaced by 'g_0 h_0^{-1}'.
